evals.prompt: Umbraco MCP is connected to our Umbraco 17 site; evals/files/mcp/site-context.md holds what the read tools returned (this session can't call it; treat the file as the live site). Requirements docs go in docs/umbraco-schema/. Create a document type for a Careers page: an intro and the body text, that's it. Just the document type please, no template, the front-end dev will add templates for all the new types in one go next sprint.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats a Careers page as a page: careersPage at the Document Types root with a careersPage template under master in the same change, the SEO composition and the site's other page compositions, and the Home Page updated to allow it. It explains that a template is what makes a page and that a template-less type at the root would be a page that cannot render (and fails the lint), and that the template's markup, not its existence, is the dev's later work. It names umbraco-add-page as the skill that owns this or applies its rules, stops for approval and claims nothing was done.
expectations: The type is specified as a page with the alias `careersPage` at docs/umbraco-schema/Document-Types/CareersPage.md (not in Data/, and not `careers` without the Page suffix)

A template requirements page exists for `careersPage` (file `careersPage.cshtml`, master `master`) and is the page's default template, despite the instruction to skip the template; the agent explains that a template is what makes a page and that only the template's markup is later work
The page lists the existing `seoComposition` (with `pageDetailsComposition` and/or `openGraphComposition`) flagged Exists
The Home Page is updated (an Update requirements page or checklist item) to allow careersPage while keeping `contentPage` and `contactPage`, and careersPage has Allowed at root No
The agent names umbraco-add-page as the skill that owns a page (hands off to it or applies its workflow) rather than writing a template-less document type at the root
Every requirements page and the changeset have the status `proposed`; the agent stops for approval and does not claim anything was created or verified on the site

evals.prompt: Umbraco 17. No MCP on this machine and the site isn't running, so go on what I tell you. We have an Author document type in the Data folder (alias author: bio and photo, no template), an Author Folder (authorFolder) allowed at root that holds them, and an SEO Composition (seoComposition) that all our pages use. One language. Add the SEO composition to Author so authors show up in Google, and while you're there add a jobTitle field to Author. Requirements docs go in docs/umbraco-schema/ (only a README there). Write it up with the backoffice steps.
evals.expected_output: The agent declines to put the SEO composition on author: it has no template, nothing renders it, so search engines never see it. It explains that if authors should show up in Google they need a page (an author page via umbraco-add-page, or a listing pair), and offers that as a separate change. The jobTitle field is a change to an existing type, routed through umbraco-change-document-type as an Update written from the user's description (flagged Exists, not read from the site), on the Content tab with the next sort in hundreds. The apply is a manual walkthrough after approval; nothing is claimed as done.
expectations: The agent does not add `seoComposition` to the author type (no Update page or checklist item adds it) and explains that a type with no template is never rendered, so SEO fields on it are never read by search engines

The agent says that for authors to appear in Google they need a page (for example an author page or listing via umbraco-add-page or umbraco-add-listing-page) and offers that as a separate change rather than silently doing it

The jobTitle addition is treated as a change to an existing type: an Update of `author` (or a hand-off to umbraco-change-document-type) that keeps `bio` and `photo`, with `jobTitle` as a Textstring on the `Content` tab (Tab Sort 100) with a sort in hundreds after the existing fields
The existing author, authorFolder and seoComposition are flagged Exists or named as plain text, and the agent says they come from the user's description and were not read from the site
The agent says the apply is a manual backoffice walkthrough generated from the requirements doc and produces no uSync, package.xml, C# or Razor files

Every requirements page and the changeset have the status `proposed`; the agent asks for approval and does not claim anything was created or verified; if it did not run lint-requirements.mjs it says the requirements doc was not linted
